name: Replace Spark Plugs
description: Replace all six spark plugs on Toyota 2GR-FE 3.5L V6 engines (transverse applications). The front bank is straightforward; the rear bank sits under the intake plenum, which has to come off. UNVERIFIED DRAFT: torque values have not been checked against a Toyota service manual - confirm them for your vehicle before relying on them.

steps.action: Let the engine cool and remove the engine cover
steps.details: Work on a cold engine: aluminium cylinder head threads are easily damaged when hot. Lift the plastic engine cover straight up off its grommets.
warnings: Never remove spark plugs from a hot aluminium head

steps.details: Loosen the terminal nut and move the cable away from the battery post. You will be unplugging sensors and the throttle body when the plenum comes off.
warnings: Radio presets and learned idle may reset

steps.action: Remove the front bank ignition coils
steps.details: On the radiator-side bank, release the connector lock and unplug each of the three coils. Remove each coil's 10mm bolt and pull the coil straight up out of the plug well.
warnings: Pull on the coil body, not the wiring
Keep track of which coil came from which cylinder

steps.action: Remove the front bank spark plugs
steps.details: Blow any debris out of the plug wells first. Remove the three plugs with a 5/8 in thin-wall plug socket and an extension.
warnings: Clear the wells before removal so debris can't fall into the cylinder

steps.action: Install new front bank spark plugs
steps.details: Thread each new plug in by hand first to avoid cross-threading, then torque to spec. The factory iridium plugs come pre-gapped (about 1.0-1.1 mm); don't try to re-gap them.

torqueSpec.note: 20 N-m. Unverified - confirm in service manual

steps.action: Reinstall the front bank ignition coils
steps.details: Push each coil fully onto its plug, install its 10mm bolt, and reconnect the connector until the lock clicks.
warnings: An unclicked connector causes a misfire

steps.details: Unplug the throttle body connector and any sensor connectors on the plenum. Disconnect the PCV and brake booster vacuum hoses. Remove the plenum's bolts, nuts and support brackets, then lift the plenum off. On some vehicles the wiper cowl must come off first for clearance.
warnings: Photograph hose and connector routing before disconnecting
Don't drop hardware into the intake ports

steps.details: Cover the open intake runners with masking tape or clean rags so nothing can fall into the engine while you work.
warnings: A dropped bolt in an intake port can destroy the engine

steps.action: Remove the rear bank ignition coils
steps.details: On the firewall-side bank, unplug and remove the three coils the same way as the front bank.
warnings: Pull on the coil body, not the wiring

steps.action: Remove the rear bank spark plugs
steps.details: Clear the plug wells, then remove the three plugs. A swivel or extra extension helps against the firewall.
warnings: Clear the wells before removal so debris can't fall into the cylinder

steps.action: Install new rear bank spark plugs
steps.details: Start each plug by hand, then torque to spec.

torqueSpec.note: 20 N-m. Unverified - confirm in service manual

steps.action: Reinstall the rear bank ignition coils
steps.details: Seat each coil, install its 10mm bolt, and reconnect the connector until the lock clicks.
warnings: An unclicked connector causes a misfire

steps.details: Remove the tape or rags from the intake ports. Fit new plenum gaskets, set the plenum in place, and tighten its fasteners evenly to the service manual torque. Reconnect every hose and connector you removed.
warnings: Use new gaskets - a vacuum leak causes rough idle and a check engine light
Count your rags: every one must come out of the ports

steps.details: Reconnect the negative battery terminal. Start the engine and listen for a smooth idle and any vacuum leak hiss, then reinstall the engine cover.
warnings: A flashing check engine light means a misfire - recheck coil connectors

reinstallNotes: Replace plugs as a full set of six. Toyota lists long-life iridium plugs for the 2GR-FE; confirm the part number and interval for your vehicle. Record the mileage and date.
